tagline: Up the switchbacks to where Idaho's gold was first found.
intro: At Greer, Idaho 11 crosses the Clearwater River and climbs 2,000 feet out of the canyon in a series of switchbacks. The grade began as a Nez Perce trail, and the Pierce gold rush gave it its first wagon roadbed in 1861. At the top, fields of grain and grass open out toward Weippe.

Past Weippe the fields give way to forest. The road runs on through Pierce, where gold was found on Orofino Creek in October 1860, and ends at Headquarters, at the edge of the Clearwater National Forest.

moments.title: Weippe Prairie
moments.text: Clark and the first of Lewis and Clark's party came starving out of the Bitterroots on the Lolo Trail onto this camas prairie in 1805, and the Nez Perce fed them.

moments.title: Pierce
moments.text: The courthouse Shoshone County built here in 1862, while Pierce was its seat and Idaho was still part of Washington Territory, is the oldest public building in Idaho.

moments.title: Headquarters
moments.text: The road ends at a Potlatch company town that began in 1906 as a fire protection station and was once the end of the line for the Camas Prairie Railroad.
